question: T12 (task-75df9d6a2c26ee21): a Text block that starts on a Scrolling block's top row follows its foot (CAP-T12BLOCKS Q). Where does it go on a big Wave Intensity fall, when moving it up by the fall would put it on row 0 or above? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a Text block added after it, made on the desktop (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/10, phone 1/2/3/10 and 3/2/5/10). Arranged by arrow keys on the selected block where a plan says so ('arr'), then the Scrolling block selected, Edit, Design ('open', a read with the panel's Wave value), two presses on Wave Intensity (179 is the press at the range's end, read as 180), Escape (let go, 'go') and two Cmd+Z, a read after each. Desktop: A 150>0, B 180>0, E 150>30, G 120>0, H 90>0, I 180>60, J 180>30, P 180>150 (one step), Q 180>90; C the Text block one row down first (2/2/4/10), 150>0; X, Y and Z both blocks two rows down first (the Scrolling block 3/2/5/26, the Text block 3/2/5/10), X 150>0, Y 180>90, Z 180>60. Phone: F, in Mobile View (the frame 428 wide) the Text block moved up two rows onto the Scrolling block's top row (1/2/3/10 there), 150>0, then back to Desktop View. R1 ran ABEGHIJPQCF and XYZ, R2 ZYXFCQP and JIHGEBA, four edit sessions. Nothing saved: every session left by Exit Without Saving.
readsAre: As CAP-T12BLOCKS: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, rowSizes, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('z' is Cmd+Z).
answer: On the desktop a fall of two steps or more moves the Text block up by as much as the foot, unless that would put it on the Scrolling block's top row or above: then it lands on the new foot, just under the block. A (1/2/3/10, 150 takes it to 4/2/6/10 and the Scrolling block to 1/2/6/26): 0 leaves the Scrolling block 1/2/2/26 and the Text block 2/2/4/10, not 0/2/2/10. B 180>0, E 150>30, G 120>0 and H 90>0 leave it at 2/2/4/10 too, the Scrolling block at 1/2/2/26.

The foot, not the row under the top: I 180>60 and J 180>30 leave the Scrolling block 1/2/3/26 and the Text block 3/2/5/10 (the plain move would give 1/2/3/10). Z, both two rows down (3/2/5/26 and 3/2/5/10): 180 takes the Text block to 7/2/9/10, 60 leaves the Scrolling block 3/2/5/26 and the Text block 5/2/7/10. X 150>0 leaves 3/2/4/26 and 4/2/6/10 (the plain move would give 2/2/4/10, above the Scrolling block's top).

When the plain move stays below the top row it is taken, the Text block still on the Scrolling block's rows: Q 180>90 leaves 1/2/4/26 and 2/2/4/10 (as CAP-T12BLOCKS Q), Y 180>90 leaves 3/2/6/26 and 4/2/6/10. C, the Text block at 2/2/4/10 (on the rows, not the top row): 150 takes it to 5/2/7/10, 0 to 2/2/4/10 (the plain move gives 1/2/3/10, the top row).
The section keeps its rows under the lowest block, by as much as that moved: A 11 to 9, C 11 to 8, I and J 12 to 10, X 11 to 9, Z 12 to 10.
A fall of one step leaves the Text block: P 180>150 takes the Scrolling block from 1/2/7/26 to 1/2/6/26 and the Text block stays at 5/2/7/10, the section at 12 rows. Not built here.

In the phone view the same block is stretched, not moved: F, both on 1/2/3/10 there, 150 takes the Scrolling block to 1/2/7/10 and the Text block to 1/2/7/10 (its top stays, its end follows the foot); 0 leaves the Scrolling block 1/2/2/10 and the Text block 1/2/7/10. The desktop areas stay. Not built here.

Escape keeps every area; Cmd+Z takes back one press at a time, both blocks and the section rows with it. R1 and R2 read alike in all 108 reads, apart from Undo and Redo at a plan's start (Redo stays on from the plan before).

Not read: a drag through such a fall (CAP-T12WAVEDRAG D: a desktop drag leaves the blocks below as the foot falls), two or more blocks on the top row, a block taller than the rows it falls through, a phone fall with the Text block moved, an imported block.

localGuesses.written: none written before the reads; ours on main moves the Text block up by the fall with no stop, 150>0 leaving it at 0/2/2/10
